propositions: Metric derivations must read raw event files for per-event or multi-occurrence data (attempts, rework windows, reopen counts) using existing reducer helpers (event_sort_key, is_active_event) rather than inventing file-listing logic, and include compaction-retired events.
Metrics requiring only a single terminal value (first_pass_rate via last_reopened_at absence, revert_recovery via reverts[]) must read compiled state from reduce_ticket rather than raw events.

attempts_per_ticket must count distinct claim sessions from open→in_progress STATUS edges; first_pass_rate must measure closed tickets never reopened; rework_within_days must measure closed→open→closed edges within n days; reopen_recovery must count tickets with any closed→open edge; revert_recovery must count reverts targeting STATUS or COMMITS events only.
Empty date ranges must return None (Unavailable in registry), while populated ranges with zero qualifying events must return measured 0.

Metrics must register into registry.py with source='structural' and confidence='high', and unit tests must verify session counting, rework day-boundaries, revert target filtering, and retired event inclusion.
